name: Turanism
summary: Turanism is the nationalist idea that the Turkic peoples, and in its Hungarian and Finnish strands the supposed Ural-Altaic kin, share an ancestral homeland (Turan) and should be united culturally and, in the long run, politically. Its Turkish mainstream, shaped by Ziya Gökalp, defines the nation by shared language and culture, wants a modern national state with secular law, a protected national economy and a solidarist order between classes, and treats Turan as a distant ideal. Racial, expansionist and militarist versions appeared in its later and Hungarian forms.
scope: The Turkish-Turkic mainstream as set out by Ziya Gökalp (Principles of Turkism, 1923; Turan poem, 1911) and pan-Turkist writers up to Enver Pasha's schemes, with the Hungarian Turan Society and post-Trianon revisionism as the main parallel. It excludes the later racial Turanism of Nihal Atsiz and the Grey Wolves, and the Finnish Fennoman strand, which would answer more authoritarian and racial questions differently. Many answers on issues Gökalp never treated are inferences and marked low.

sources.usedFor: Gökalp's definition of nation, Islam, Durkheimian solidarism and primacy of group over individual, homogeneous state.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism has society's surplus profits fund shelters, schools and care for the poor, sick and disabled, so a state-backed health guarantee fits, though he never names healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from solidarism's aim to end destitution and the welfare of workers and peasants; no wage policy is stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Gökalp calls free-market economics a national system of industrial Britain and wants a guided national economy instead.

public-ownership.rationale: Gökalp holds that there must be 'social property' beside private property, with society-owned factories and estates and a national electricity grid.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Surplus profit not earned by individual labour belongs to society, implying heavy claims on large gains, but he wants taxes to fall once public enterprises thrive.

unions-good.rationale: He wants national guilds and federations of professional groups with their own ethics and sanctions, a favourable view of organised occupational bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property is legitimate only if it serves social solidarity, and forms that do not may be rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from solidarism and the rule that profit from society's effort belongs to society; no corporate regulation is discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Solidarism's goal is to end all destitution and provide for the poor, orphans, widows and sick, so cutting welfare runs against it.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejects collectivism and proposes social property run on society's behalf, not ownership by each firm's workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the movement's statist, security-minded nationalism; no source addresses surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on national morality and discipline; no source addresses drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Sources do not address the issue and adherents' likely views run both ways.

strong-leader.rationale: Turanist movements around Enver Pasha and the CUP favoured decisive leadership, though Gökalp himself stressed popular sovereignty.

state-harmful.rationale: Gökalp builds the programme on a modern national state and its public enterprises; the Turan ideal is itself a state-building aim.

limit-guns.rationale: No source addresses gun control and adherents would not be united.

empower-police-military.rationale: Turkism entered through the military academies and the movement's heroes are warriors; Gökalp praises heroism and discipline.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's emphasis on family ethics and national morality.

decide-locally.rationale: Gökalp wants a national economy to replace regional ones and national guilds to replace town guilds, favouring national over local authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear Turanist line.

traditional-family.rationale: Gökalp treats the family as the social cell and devotes a section to family ethics, though he rejects patriarchal sovereignty in favour of a 'paternal' family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its stress on family ethics and national tradition; unaddressed in sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pro-natal bent of Turanist nationalism, which aims to unite 'one hundred million Turks'.

more-religion-public.rationale: Gökalp counts Islam as part of Turkish identity and wants the Quran taught but also strips law of clericalism; adherents are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No source supports it and ethnic-nationalist movements generally resist group redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gökalp stresses sociological upbringing for nationality but says nothing on gender; inferred as against.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Gökalp says culture is national, wants the Turkish culture preserved among the people to be revived, and makes it the nation's basis.

gradual-change.rationale: Gökalp seeks moderation between conservatives and radicals yet urges full adoption of Western civilisation, so adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from its call for a culturally homogeneous nation-state; immigration itself is not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Gökalp expects Turkey to be the most sincere member of a real League of Nations, but this is a passing remark.

free-trade.rationale: Gökalp argues free trade suits industrial Britain and would leave others economically enslaved, urging protection instead.

nation-first.rationale: Gökalp's programme puts the nation's culture, economy and interests first, while keeping a vision of peaceful international morality.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; Gökalp praises international morality but the movement's stress on sovereignty cuts the other way.

open-borders.rationale: A nation defined by shared language and culture, with a homogeneous state, sits poorly with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Gökalp wants Turkey to become a centre of large-scale industry; inferred strongly against limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No source addresses it; the movement predates the issue.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Gökalp values Western science and industry as the means of modernisation, but never claims they solve most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the pro-industrialisation, power-seeking outlook; unaddressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Turanists supported the 1908 CUP revolution but Gökalp favoured moderation; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Gökalp wants professional bodies freed from general authority so that competence of specialists governs their fields.

central-planning.rationale: He wants a state-aided national economy but rejects collectivism, preferring solidarism with private property alongside social property.

socialized-markets.rationale: His mix of private and social property is not a market-socialist model, and he never states a view on markets owned by workers or the public.

land-value-tax.rationale: Society keeps unearned surplus, but there is no single-tax proposal; not addressed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the rule that wealth not due to individual labour belongs to society.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare is through public institutions and shelters, not cash payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Gökalp says a national economy and large industry can only come through protection, citing List's national economics.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Social surplus is to capitalise public factories and estates and a general electricity network under a national economic programme.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He wants large-scale industry and social property over small trades, and calls the old regional small-craft economy obsolete.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Gökalp attacks socialists and communists for trying to abolish private property and keeps the existing economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from his state-guided national economy; central banking is not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: His national guilds and professional federations, with solidarism between groups, resemble corporatism, though wage-setting is not spelled out.

one-party-rule.rationale: Gökalp called Turkism a school of thought rather than a party and drew up a Republican People's party programme; Turanists are split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Gökalp says modern states give no family special privilege and treats the sultanate as a medieval form.

democracy-best.rationale: Gökalp defines the modern state as democracy and calls the ancient Turks the most democratic people, though some Turanist movements were authoritarian.

direct-votes.rationale: He wants people sovereign but represented through professional federations; direct legislation is not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejects class rule and Marxism; representation through guilds of all professions is not council power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nations should have states, but Turanists resist breaking up the nation-state, and the sources do not endorse a right to secede.

natural-rulers.rationale: Gökalp requires every member of the nation to be equal with no special class privileges.

political-violence-never.rationale: Turanists like Enver Pasha waged war and revolt; inferred as not pacifist.

war-builds-character.rationale: Gökalp assigns Turks a mission of heroism and self-sacrifice, though he insists ancient Turks were peaceful.

separate-church-state.rationale: Gökalp wants law freed of theocracy and clericalism while keeping Islam as national heritage.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He says laws must be freed from theocracy and clericalism, and legislation belongs to the people.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A modern national state with its own legal system and public enterprises leaves no room for private defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the movement's military roots and the Turan ideal; Gökalp does not state it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Gökalp holds that each culture-nation should have its own state and calls multi-nation empires an error, though he defines nation by culture, not blood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Gökalp devotes a chapter to refuting Marx's historical materialism with Durkheim's idealist sociology.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He wants equality before the law and no privileged class, not equal results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No source addresses it; inferred from a unitary nation-state outlook.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; Gökalp's grievances target capitulations, not payments.

civilizational-union.rationale: Turanism unites by Turkic kinship; Gökalp explicitly rejects uniting by faith as 'ümmet' and a Muslim-wide nation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism and sociology place duty to the community above individual interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Gökalp argues group life outweighs the individual, who becomes a real person only by representing the culture.

limit-population.rationale: Turanism values numbers, citing a hundred million Turks as an inspiration.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Gökalp wants Turkey to build large-scale industry and enter Western civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He wants rapid adoption of Western science but respect for national culture; no stance on disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: No Turanist source discusses bodily enhancement, and Gökalp's focus is cultural, so there is no basis for a side.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from its culture-centred, community view of politics.

restore-past-order.rationale: Gökalp rejects restoring Ottoman order and urges full entry into Western civilisation, while reviving folk culture.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He treats Turkism as a scientific school yet is programmatic; no clear stance.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred; Turanist programmes work through education, associations and state power.

means-match-ends.rationale: Turanist sources set out aims and organisation but never discuss whether methods must mirror ends, so adherents are indifferent.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Gökalp's programme demands modern large industry and Western civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gökalp follows Durkheim in valuing the division of labour as the basis of modern solidarity and organised professions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Solidarism cares for the needy but does not adopt communism's distribution rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Solidarism keeps private enterprise yet wants public enterprise for welfare; split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He rejects Marx and holds that classes cooperate; only surplus not earned by labour belongs to society.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Gökalp criticises Marxism's idea that the working class must eliminate other classes and defines 'the people' as all who accept legal equality.

collective-farming.rationale: He rejects collectivism and keeps private property under solidarism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Gökalp denies Marx's economic determinism but does criticise European imperialism; weakly against.

taxation-theft.rationale: He expects taxes to be reduced by public wealth, not abolished, and treats the state as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Gökalp subordinates the individual to national culture and solidarity, not liberal limits.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Gökalp criticises liberal individualism and says group life outweighs the individual.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the movement's military roots and nationalism; unaddressed in sources.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from nationalist and solidarist belonging; unaddressed.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from solidarism and public enterprise.

positive-liberty.rationale: Solidarism ties freedom to welfare and the end of destitution, though it uses other terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: No Turanist source claims universities and media outrank elected officials; Gökalp himself was an academic who wanted scholars' professional autonomy.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Gökalp argues no pure races exist and that traits are acquired through society, though the Turanist movement included racialist writers.

organic-representation.rationale: Gökalp proposes guilds federated up to a national general assembly of professional delegates.

total-state.rationale: He wants professional bodies autonomous from general state authority, and culture as the nation's own, not state-directed.

national-rebirth.rationale: Turan was a redemptive ideal after the Balkan defeat, and Gökalp wants a national awakening, but he frames it as cultural revival rather than a radical break.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Gökalp calls Turan a distant ideal and says ancient Turks were not imperialists, whereas Enver Pasha pursued military pan-Turanian schemes.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Gökalp's modern state rests on popular sovereignty and legal equality, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: No individual, family or class may hold special privileges.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Gökalp holds positive sciences are international and independent of religion.

universal-morality.rationale: Gökalp treats morality as sociological and national, from national ethics up to a wider civilised morality, with no single reason-given code.

single-common-good.rationale: Solidarism seeks general welfare and cooperation between groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Turanist sources do not address it, and Hungarian Turanism had antisemitic strands while Gökalp's did not.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Turanism seeks unity of kin peoples across borders, and post-Trianon Hungarian Turanists sought reunion of Magyars abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: Gökalp's Linguistic Turkism urges reviving old Turkish words and purifying the language, though Turkish was never out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Solidarism sets cooperation between groups, not worker control; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from a national education system that transmits culture.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Gökalp's economics concerns protection and social property, not deficit policy, so the ideology is indifferent to this question.

economic-freedom.rationale: Gökalp rejects free-trade liberalism and has a guided national economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gökalp stresses law made by the people and institutions, not rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Gökalp's central claim is that each culture-nation deserves its own national state, as the Turks now have.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty-first, military outlook of Turanists; unaddressed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Gökalp treats religion and national ideals as sacred social realities.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Solidarism is a national community scheme; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the solidarity ethic of reciprocal work and mutual support.

class-collaboration.rationale: Solidarism is Gökalp's chosen system: groups cooperate in mutual support rather than conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Gökalp wants national heritage collected and brought to the fore, and old arts revived.

dominated-front.rationale: Turanism aimed at counterweights to Western and Russian influence, though Gökalp himself wanted Western civilisation.

workers-nation.rationale: Gökalp ties workers to national guilds and the nation, not an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gökalp says feminism is democracy applied to women and claims Turkic women held equal standing.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and Muslim Turkists would differ.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Gökalp defines nation by culture and upbringing and denies pure races; segregation law conflicts with legal equality.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He sees the state as the organ of the nation as a whole and denies class war.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Gökalp says nationality is acquired by upbringing, joining the national culture, and the modern state should be culturally homogeneous.

elite-replacement.rationale: No source supports a replacement theory in Turanism.

proportional-representation.rationale: His own proposal is occupational, not party-list; no stance on party proportionality.

national-mission.rationale: Gökalp gives each nation its own mission, with the Turkish one moral, not spreading a government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gökalp attacks the patriarchal family as alien yet later strands differ.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Gökalp wants the elite to go 'towards the people', but no corruption charge is central.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed, and Gökalp's social view of traits opposes biological policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from defensive nationalism; adherents contested Armenian-related accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Gökalp's state builds public industry, social services, schools and museums.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Gökalp stresses that all peoples are mixed and that nationality is cultural, not blood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Gökalp requires legal equality of all nation members, though Turanism ranks nations by cultural attachment.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Gökalp's Legal Turkism calls for a modern civil code and equality of all before the law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; Gökalp's stress on culture rather than faith suggests no restriction.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Pastoral Turkic culture and Muslim practice make such a ban alien; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Gökalp wanted the Quran taught in schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Gökalp says the powers of law-making and government belong directly to the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionism and a national industrial economy suggest export-led aims, but he does not state it.

population-transfer.rationale: Turanist sources do not endorse it, though the CUP wartime policies are linked to the movement by critics.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Turanism includes militant strands, so a strict ban on initiating force is unlikely.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement drew on social Darwinism, per the pan-Turkism article, though Gökalp's own stress is solidarity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred, order-minded outlook; unaddressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican idea of freedom as non-domination is absent from Turanist writing, which treats freedom in national terms.

separated-powers.rationale: Gökalp wants autonomous professional authorities but says nothing on separation among state branches.

vanguard-party.rationale: Gökalp rejects Marxism and Lenin's route, taking solidarism and national culture as the guide.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Gökalp's social ideal includes ending destitution and shelters for poor, orphans and sick, recalling the khan who 'made the poor rich'.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed anywhere in Turanist sources, and solidarism could support either public or private homes.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from solidarism's class cooperation over conflict.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Gökalp blames social causes such as capitulations and backwardness, and wants more Turks.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Gökalp holds that a modern state must be homogeneous in culture, religion and national identity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Gökalp's model is election of delegates through guilds.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from order-minded nationalism and the wartime CUP; unaddressed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from a guided national economy and welfare orientation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not stated; Gökalp favoured professional autonomy and free inquiry in a modern state.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the nation-state ideal where the army serves the national state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the cultural basis of nationality, which takes upbringing to acquire.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representation pay is never addressed in Gökalp or the movement's other writings, so the ideology is indifferent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the CUP was disciplined but Gökalp did not set a rule.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Turanism seeks a union of kin peoples, not pooling with unrelated nations as in the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Turanist sources describe no preference between presidential and parliamentary command of the army or the choice of ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Sunni Islam has no bishops, and Gökalp wanted clerical authority checked.

clerical-rule.rationale: Gökalp explicitly condemns clericalism and theocracy as medieval features that national law must drop.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Turkism is nationalist and puts the nation's interests first; it rejects the internationalist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Gökalp wants national art but proposes revival, not censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed by Gökalp or by the movement, and the CUP and later Turanists acted differently in practice.

recall-officials.rationale: Gökalp wanted popular sovereignty but never proposed recalling elected officials, so the ideology has no stated view.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Hungarian Turanists sought alliances with Turkey, Japan and others, and pan-Turkists courted German backing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; private property under solidarism makes a ban unlikely.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred; the movement was tied to professional military academies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Gökalp holds the villagers and common people kept the authentic culture, though he wants large industry as well.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Turan ideal unites Turks split among states, and Hungarian Turanists after Trianon sought to reunite Magyars.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Gökalp urges the elite to go 'towards the people' because they have lost contact with national culture.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Gökalp sees Western civilisation as the one to adopt and ancient Turkic morality as highest, not as only different.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not addressed; Gökalp backs feminism and equality but also family ethics and Islamic heritage, so adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Gökalp champions positive science and Durkheim's sociology.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Turanism's kin-based unity favours descent, though Gökalp's nationality rests on upbringing.

minority-language-support.rationale: A culturally homogeneous national state implies one national language; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Gökalp wants uniform law for all and equality before it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Gökalp's culture is a shared whole, and an individual becomes real only by representing it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He criticises capitulations but does not address debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Gökalp argues free trade would leave nations economically enslaved, so independence requires a national economy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from popular sovereignty over making law.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Gökalp wants both democracy and fast industrialisation; adherents split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Gökalp's international morality speaks of mutual generosity between nations, but no aid duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and strength emphasis.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How the head of state is chosen is not addressed in Turanist writings, so the ideology has no settled view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from a guided national economy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Irredentist nationalism resists ceding claimed homeland, seen in Hungarian Trianon revisionism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Gökalp states that private property is legitimate provided it serves social solidarity.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Marxist debate not addressed; Turanists opposed the Soviets for other reasons.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy lies outside what Gökalp or the Turanist movement discussed, so the ideology is indifferent.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred; Turanists sought alliances of kin peoples.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from national self-determination and irredentist concern for kin in lost territory.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Gökalp wants clericalism and theocracy removed from law, putting religious authority under national law.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the nation-state ideal and Turanists' resistance to splitting the nation.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy with a separate legal and economic order is not discussed, and Turanists favour a unified national state and national economy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Turanist sources do not discuss a ceremonial head of state, and the CUP leaders were openly partisan, so adherents are split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Gökalp rejects theocracy, explicitly criticising sultans regarded as shadows of God on earth.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Solidarism implies progressive burdens; not stated.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gökalp argues individuals are born asocial and acquire language, morals and religion from society.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He says authority and law belong to the people, and that rulers' privileges are medieval.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is an anachronism for a movement of the early twentieth century, with no source giving a view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Gökalp's modern state rejects class privilege and favours popular sovereignty.

leader-cult.rationale: Gökalp opposes sacred rulers, but later Turanist movements cultivated hero figures.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules after separation are not addressed by Gökalp or the movement, so the ideology is indifferent.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Turan, the union of kin peoples, is the movement's defining aim, stated by Gökalp as the ultimate ideal of Turkism and by Hungarian Turanists as kinship with the East.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism and class conflict in favour of solidarism between classes.

land-redistribution.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism accepts property under national interest and cared for the peasantry, but no land seizure programme is stated; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Hungarian Turanism's post-Trianon revisionism and kin solidarity suggest support for return of displaced co-nationals; not stated directly.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hungarian Turanism fed Trianon revisionism and pan-Turkism sought Turkic lands under one rule, though Gökalp narrowed the claim to a distant ideal.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Gökalp wanted secular law and a national, not religious, basis for the state, so criminal penalties for leaving a faith do not fit.

women-must-cover.rationale: Gökalp's modernist programme of secular law and reformed family ethics does not call for compulsory covering; inferred from that programme.

common-currency.rationale: Turan implies eventual union but a shared currency is never discussed, and Gökalp wanted a protected national economy; inferred indifference.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Gökalp wanted a culturally homogeneous nation defined by language and culture, not self-governing minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Turanists look to kin unity and the national homeland rather than minorities staying put to win rights; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism and held that shared culture and the group's collective conscience shape society, not modes of production.

ban-cartels.rationale: Gökalp proposed guilds and a solidarist, corporatist economy under national direction, which conflicts with an anti-concentration competition programme; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: A protected, state-guided national economy would support rescuing national firms; inferred from Gökalp's economic nationalism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Gökalp put the nation's collective will above the individual, which fits majority rule without liberal limits; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gökalp backed women's role in the family and public life but nothing in the sources supports mandatory parity; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Gökalp advocated protectionism and a national economy and rejected free trade, though a fully closed bloc with colonies is not stated.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A protectionist outlook wants trade governed by national interest and the sources show no view on binding labour or environmental clauses.

moral-incentives.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism puts group duty above individual interest, but he kept property and economic incentives, so this is inferred and weak.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Enver Pasha's conspiratorial schemes were militarist, but Gökalp's mainstream favoured cultural work and a national state; adherents split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Gökalp built the nation on language and culture and supported national sovereignty over dynasty; the Republic abolished the sultanate; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Gökalp's Turkism builds education on national culture and language, so history is taught centred on the Turkish nation and its Turkic past.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's nationalism stresses each nation's own culture and a modern national state, and Turanists opposed Western domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Gökalp wanted national education that instils national culture, ideals and loyalty to the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Turanism never addressed the issue and nationalists differ; Gökalp's culture-based nation is open to assimilation, which cuts both ways.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarist, protected national economy accepts a large state role, though he never discussed money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarism assumes class conflict can be harmonised within the nation, not that capitalism must collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pan-Turkists and Hungarian Turanists sought cultural and political influence among kin peoples in lands of the former Ottoman and Hungarian realms.

delink-world-market.rationale: Gökalp wanted a protected national economy built up through national capital, not a break with the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarism denies that classes exploit each other within the nation, so a labour-aristocracy thesis has no place.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarism and national state favour regulated, communal order over unrestricted private choice.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Gökalp favoured modern secular law, but Turanism never addressed entrenched rights and its authoritarian strands rejected limits on the nation's will.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Turanists, Hungarian revisionists above all, treated the post-1918 partitions and the division of Turkic peoples under Russian rule as unjust; inferred, as no statement on treaties is quoted.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's national-sovereignty nation-state; the mainstream did not insist on dynastic rule, though he never wrote a doctrine of elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Gökalp gives the group primacy over the individual and wants a homogeneous national state, so a single dissenter would not bind the nation; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's modern secular-law national state; he did not discuss a right of resistance directly.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Gökalp's programme is a modern national state under national sovereignty; inferred, since he left the parliament question to the Republic's practice.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: ordinary humane attitudes, with no Turanist text on animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the pastoral and agrarian Turkic tradition of using animals, with no stated position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism has society's surplus profits fund shelters, schools and care for the poor, so duty runs from the better-off to the needy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Turanism is an activist nationalist mission and Gökalp put the group above the individual, so withdrawal from public life is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism and held that culture is the nation's own living core, not an instrument of class order; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxist class analysis in favour of solidarism between classes, so he would not frame power as class domination by consent; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Gökalp's protectionist national economy answers the Ottoman capitulations and foreign economic dominance; inferred as the closest match.

native-born-offices.rationale: A national state defined by shared language and culture would reserve public posts for members of the nation; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Turanists looked to their own national road, not to foreign direction, though they rejected socialism itself; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Gökalp's programme is a protected national economy built on national capital and rejects free trade.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Hungarian Turanism was driven by Trianon revisionism, while Gökalp's Turkish mainstream held Turan as a distant ideal; the strands lean toward yes.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Strands split: Gökalp's nation is cultural and assimilating, Hungarian and racial strands stress ethnic primacy; the issue is anachronistic.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Turkish mainstream is a nationalist movement later tied to the far right (Atsiz); an anti-fascist founding value is not part of its programme; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism but wrote before fascism, and later Turanists drew on fascist models; adherents are split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the statement is outside Turanism, and a nationalist adherent would likely take the standard reading that slavery was the cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reverence for the ancestral past and national memory is a Turanist theme (Orkhon inscriptions, Red Apple); inferred for monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gökalp argued for women's equality in the family and in public life, so equal attention to men's issues is plausible; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by Turanism; Gökalp's family ethics favour women's protection and equality, so adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Gökalp separated Western technical civilization, to be adopted, from national culture, to be preserved, and wanted institutions fitted to the nation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Young Turk officers like Enver Pasha pursued Turanian schemes by military means; later Republican practice rejected a political army; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Gökalp's family ethics keep a traditional domestic order; no recognition of care work as paid labour is stated.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarist view of society values family and community bonds.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp wanted a modern national state with elected institutions and did not address examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Its mainstream backs a protected national economy against foreign dominance.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's support for secular law and women's rights in a modern national state.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: a modern national state favours regular representative institutions, not instructed delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the solidarist order between classes, which favours shared over purely individual provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's national economy does not call for communal land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the modern national state it supports, which is an elected constitutional one.

single-official-language.rationale: Turkism defines the nation by shared language and culture, so one common language is central.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its protective national economy and nationalism, which favour keeping land in national hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: nationalists of this strand see rights as the nation's shared status, not group outcome tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: Gökalp's solidarism is not an attack on consumption, nor a defence of it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Enver Pasha's schemes for backing Turkic movements against rival powers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: Turan is a cultural ideal and the mainstream does not endorse forcing allies by arms.

corporate-influence.rationale: Gökalp wanted class solidarity and a national economy, but never addressed corporate lobbying; inferred as neutral.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's protectionism and national economy and his wariness of foreign economic control.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from his emphasis on family ethics and the nation's strength; population policy is not stated.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; the national economy favours national over foreign owners but local authority powers are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from solidarism, which makes society responsible for work and livelihood of workers and peasants; no guarantee is stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Turanists value national unity of kin peoples over regime type, and the sources do not tie peace to democracy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Gökalp put the group above the individual and treated national law and duty as binding on members.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: pan-Turkism aimed at uniting kin peoples across borders, which implies a right to act beyond them.

industrial-unions.rationale: Gökalp favoured guilds and professional corporations by occupation, which fits craft or trade groups more than industry unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream defines the nation by language and culture; racial and conspiratorial versions came in later and Hungarian strands outside the scope.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Gökalp's family ethics and Durkheimian view of the family treat it as the base of the nation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from his state-centred, group-first, homogeneous national state; transparency is not addressed.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from his protectionist national economy, which favours national over distant sources; local scale is not discussed.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gökalp built guilds, a national state and Turan societies; organised, permanent institutions are central.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from his secular national law and nationalism, which put the national state first.

religious-nation.rationale: Gökalp defined the nation by language and culture, not by race or religion alone, though Islam remained part of Turkish culture.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Gokalp pictured Turkic kin uniting as a nation of equals, not a tribute system; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Gokalp wanted a unified national state with solidarist sharing between classes, so regional retention fits poorly; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Gokalp accepted private property within a solidarist order and rejected Marxism, so common ownership of production is not his line.

defeat-communism.rationale: Turkist writers opposed Marxism and Russian power, but a campaign to defeat communism is not stated; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Gokalp favoured a protected national economy with guilds and state guidance, which does not fit open private provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Gokalp treated religion as a lasting social and cultural bond of the nation, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Gokalp wanted national industry and capital and rejected Marxism, which suggests a positive view of capitalist development; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Gokalp backed women gaining family rights through reform of law and ethics, not economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Gokalp stressed family ethics and the family as a social unit, so domestic work stays private; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic Turkism calls for replacing Arabic and Persian borrowings with old Turkish words.

treaties-binding.rationale: Gokalp wanted a homogeneous national state, so entrenched treaties with internal nations do not fit; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Gokalp promoted cooperatives and guilds within a national state, not self-governing communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: The Turkish mainstream sought a culturally homogeneous nation-state, so settlement policy fits; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Gokalp rejected both Marxism and free-market liberalism in favour of solidarism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Turan as an ancestral homeland implies a historical-kin claim, but Gökalp made it a distant ideal and the sources do not state a general rule.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Gökalp died before the Holocaust and the Turkish mainstream did not deny it; inferred from his rejection of race-based theory.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's conservative family ethics.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Gökalp put the group above the individual and favoured a homogeneous nation-state, which inferred fits curbing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Gökalp wanted secular law and separated nation from religion, so blasphemy punishment is not a state task.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from Turkish anti-imperial national-economy outlook; colonial rule is not addressed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Gökalp put the nation ahead of the Islamic community, so a universal duty of defence is inferred as unsupported.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Gökalp's programme calls for secular law and a modern national state with religion as a private matter.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Gökalp's guilds and solidarism give vocational groups a voice, inferred as a form of participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism and class struggle and put national solidarity first.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Gökalp's family ethics and the conservative character of the movement.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from conservative family ethics and national-population concerns.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism rejected both free trade and Marxism, a combining approach, though adherents are not explicit.

alienated-labor.rationale: Gökalp rejected Marxism and held that wage work serves national solidarity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Gökalp wanted Turks to adopt Western civilisation while keeping Islam as national culture, so incompatibility is inferred as rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Gökalp grounded authority in the nation, not in divine law.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Gökalp's secular state and the Republic's Kemalist line are inferred to bar religious dress in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and no principle bears directly on it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism and protected national economy sit between laissez-faire and state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pan-Turkism under Enver Pasha and the Turan ideal assume military power.

rich-first.rationale: Gökalp's solidarism opposes inequality between classes but protectionism nurtured a national bourgeoisie; inferred as split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Enver Pasha allied with Germany while the Republic broke with Turanism and stayed neutral; adherents were split.

missingStatements.text: Peoples who share a language family and ancestry should work toward political unity across existing borders.
missingStatements.rationale: Turan, the union of kin peoples, is the movement's defining aim, stated by Gökalp as the ultimate ideal of Turkism and by Hungarian Turanists as kinship with the East.

missingStatements.text: A nation's language should be purified of foreign words and its older vocabulary revived.
missingStatements.rationale: Gökalp's Linguistic Turkism is a core programme item calling for replacing Arabic and Persian borrowings with old Turkish words.
missingStatements.declined: Linguistic purism is narrow to Turkish language reform; revive-national-language covers the nearby question.

missingStatements.text: A nation's tradition is better represented by its pre-religious ancestral past than by its recent history.
missingStatements.rationale: Gökalp and Turanists draw on pre-Islamic Turkic khanates, the Sky God religion and Orkhon inscriptions as the authentic national culture and Red Apple memory.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to national-origin myths of Turkism; no common axis other ideologies could take a side on.

notes: Gökalp himself narrowed Turan to Turkic peoples and called it a long-term cultural ideal, and the Turkish Republic rejected pan-Turkism; Hungarian Turanism was more racial and Trianon-driven and Atsiz's strand was racist, so answers on race, expansion and authoritarianism differ by strand. Gökalp's own quoted lines stress language, culture and religion over race.
